name: Sonaar MP3 Audio Player Cloud
author: sonaar

sections.description:
Add an MP3 audio player to your WordPress pages with Sonaar Cloud. Create music playlists, showcase podcast episodes, and customize your player with templates, artwork, waveforms and playback controls. Use the Gutenberg block, Elementor widget or a shortcode to place your player on your website.

Built by Sonaar Music, Sonaar MP3 Audio Player Cloud connects your WordPress editor to a hosted audio library and visual player designer. Open Studio to create or edit a player, then preview it on your page.

A Sonaar Cloud account and an internet connection are required. Start with the free plan for up to 10 tracks and three saved players. Uploaded audio and player designs are managed through the hosted service. Larger libraries and additional hosted features are available on paid plans.

Explore Sonaar Cloud for WordPress

Gutenberg, Elementor and shortcode support

  • Gutenberg audio player: insert the Sonaar MP3 Audio Player Cloud block, connect your account, and create or select a player. Edit it from the block toolbar or sidebar and preview the result in the editor.
  • Elementor audio player: add the native Sonaar MP3 Audio Player Cloud widget, marked with a purple CLOUD ribbon. Use its controls to choose a player and open Studio. Elementor Pro is not required.
  • Audio player shortcode: embed a saved player in the Classic Editor, a Shortcode block or another builder that supports WordPress shortcodes. The Sonaar plugin must be installed and active.

Music playlists and podcast episodes

Present an album, a music portfolio, a beat collection, podcast episodes or voice demos with a player built around your audio. Select individual tracks or use collections and categories from your Sonaar library to build a playlist.

Add track titles, artist names and cover artwork so listeners can identify what is playing. Use one saved player on several pages, or create separate players for different playlists.

Player templates, artwork and waveforms

Choose a template in Sonaar Cloud Studio and customize its colors, artwork, layout and playback controls. Configure the tracklist and waveform or progress display to suit your content. Responsive players adapt to the available space, with automatic height or a manual height setting in WordPress.

Save a design once and reuse it across your website. Changes saved to that cloud player appear wherever the same player is embedded. Duplicate the player in Studio when you want an independent version.

Assign audio to posts, pages and custom post types

Give each page its own song or ordered playlist while reusing a player design. A site administrator sets up Posts, Pages or a supported public custom post type through Sonaar > Set up a new player.

  • Choose a shared player design and insert it automatically before or after the page content.
  • Alternatively, use an existing Gutenberg block or Elementor widget and enable Use this page’s audio. Each block or widget keeps its selected design and plays the current page’s assigned tracks.
  • Search your Sonaar library or upload audio from the WordPress editor, then arrange the page’s playlist and save the page.
  • Manage existing page assignments together and review title-based matching suggestions before applying them.

Audio stays hosted by Sonaar Cloud and counts toward your account’s track allowance. Assignments use WordPress post IDs, so changing a page title or permalink keeps its audio association. This workflow assigns audio to existing content; it does not create WordPress posts.

Sticky audio player and playback between pages

Enable the sticky bar to keep playback controls at the bottom of your published website. Enable Continuous Player in Sonaar Cloud to remember the current track and playback position as visitors move between pages in the same browser tab, including pages without a player block.

Full-page navigation briefly interrupts audio while the next page loads, and browser autoplay rules may require another click on Play. Uninterrupted playback requires a compatible AJAX navigation setup. The plugin does not add AJAX navigation to your theme.

Audio library, collections and listener analytics

Open Dashboard from WordPress to manage your audio library, collections, categories and workspace settings. Upload audio to Sonaar Cloud and reuse it in your players and page assignments. Listener analytics are available according to your Sonaar plan and playback analytics settings.

Studio opens inside an editor dialog, with a separate-window option when needed. Billing and account administration open separately on Sonaar.

Free account and hosted service requirements

The WordPress plugin is free to install. Sonaar Cloud provides the account, audio hosting, player designer and player delivery. Its free plan includes up to 10 tracks and three saved players; paid plans offer more capacity and additional service features.

WordPress stores player references and page-audio assignments. Uploaded audio and player settings stay on Sonaar Cloud rather than in your WordPress Media Library. Published players need access to the hosted service to load and play.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins > Add New Plugin, search for Sonaar MP3 Audio Player Cloud, then install and activate it. To install a downloaded ZIP, use Upload Plugin instead.
  2. Add the Sonaar MP3 Audio Player Cloud block or the Sonaar MP3 Audio Player Cloud Elementor widget to a page.
  3. Click Connect Sonaar Cloud, sign in or create an account, and approve the connection.
  4. Create a player, choose a template and add your tracks, or select an existing player. Save changes in Studio, then save or update your WordPress page.

For a shortcode, insert a Shortcode block and paste [sonaar_cloud_player id="PLAYER-UUID"], replacing PLAYER-UUID with your saved player’s ID.

Elementor is optional. Use Gutenberg or a shortcode if Elementor is not installed.

If you installed an earlier development build under a different folder or main plugin filename, deactivate that copy before installing this ZIP. Activate the new copy and open a page with an existing player to verify it. Deleting the old plugin through WordPress can clear the local account connection. Connect Sonaar Cloud again if WordPress asks you to. Your saved player references and cloud content carry over.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Sonaar Cloud account? Is there a free plan?

Yes, an account is required to connect WordPress, manage audio and create players. The plugin is free to install, and Sonaar Cloud has a free plan with up to 10 tracks and three saved players. Paid plans provide more capacity and additional hosted features. See Sonaar Cloud for current plan details.

Where are my audio files hosted?

Files uploaded in Studio are hosted by Sonaar Cloud, rather than your WordPress Media Library. Supported external audio URLs continue to use their original hosting. Playback requires access to those services.

Does the audio player work with Elementor Free?

Yes. The native widget works with Elementor Free; Elementor Pro is not required. Elementor itself is optional: the Gutenberg block and shortcode also work without it.

Can each post or page play different audio with the same design?

Yes. Set up the post type through Sonaar > Set up a new player, then assign a song or playlist in each page’s Sonaar Audio Player settings. Choose automatic placement with a shared design, or enable Use this page’s audio on your Gutenberg block or Elementor widget. That block or widget retains its own selected design. In an Elementor template, the preview page supplies the audio.

Does the player work on mobile? Can I adjust its height?

Players adapt to their container width. Automatic height is enabled by default so the embed can follow its content. Turn it off in the block or widget settings to choose a fixed height, or use the shortcode attributes below. Preview your chosen template at the widths used by your site.

Can I manage my library without leaving WordPress?

Yes. Open Dashboard to access Audio Library, including Collections, Audio and Categories, along with analytics and workspace settings. Billing and account administration open separately.

How do I use the shortcode?

With this plugin installed and active, copy the player’s UUID from its Sonaar embed URL and use:

[sonaar_cloud_player id="PLAYER-UUID"]

For a fixed height:

[sonaar_cloud_player id="PLAYER-UUID" height="520" auto_height="false"]

Automatic height is enabled by default. Manual height accepts 180 to 2000 pixels. An optional title attribute supplies the player’s accessible title.

What happens when I edit or duplicate a player?

Saving an existing player updates the same cloud player wherever it is embedded. Duplicating a WordPress block or Elementor widget keeps that reference. Use Duplicate player in Studio when you want an independent design or playlist. WordPress revisions restore the reference, not an earlier version of the cloud player.

Does playback continue when visitors change pages?

Enable Continuous Player in your Sonaar Cloud workspace settings and enable the player’s sticky bar. The plugin remembers the track, playback position, paused state, volume and playback speed in the same browser tab, and resumes on the next page even if it has no player. No extra Sonaar script is needed in WordPress.

Normal full-page navigation briefly interrupts audio while the destination loads. Browsers may require visitors to press Play to resume. Uninterrupted playback requires a compatible AJAX navigation setup; enabling Continuous Player does not turn your theme into an AJAX website.

What if Studio does not open?

Try again or use Open Studio in a new window. Allow the connection popup if your browser blocks it. Save unsaved work before switching windows. If the connection has expired or been revoked, connect your account again.

Can every WordPress user edit my Sonaar account?

No. Each WordPress user connects their own Sonaar identity. WordPress checks editing permissions, and Sonaar checks access to the connected workspace.

Is this the same as MP3 Audio Player by Sonaar?

This is the Sonaar Cloud integration. It does not replace or automatically convert players created with the separate MP3 Audio Player by Sonaar plugin.

What happens if I disconnect or uninstall?

Disconnect revokes this WordPress user’s editing connection. Uninstall removes local connection credentials but does not revoke the cloud grant remotely; disconnect first to revoke it immediately. Neither action deletes cloud audio or unpublishes cloud players. Removing the plugin removes its WordPress rendering functionality. Manage cloud content and publication from your Sonaar account.
sections.changelog:
1.0.2 – November 13, 2026

  • Improved playlist selection and drag-and-drop responsiveness with background saves and fewer library requests.
  • Improved player preview readiness and prevented late loading events from hiding an already rendered player.
  • Reduced repeated library refreshes and playlist saves when uploading multiple audio files.
  • Prevented overlapping account connection checks on slow networks.
  • Fixed the selected-track checkmark appearance in the audio picker.

1.0.1 – November 12, 2026

  • Fixed the first-install screen to offer account connection without showing a request failure. Genuine service errors remain visible.
